fib: ______ is the law which regulates competition amongst undertakings in a market.
Competition law
Competition law is the law which regulates competition amongst undertakings in a market.
______ is a market where there is one seller with lots of buyers.
monopoly
Monopoly A monopoly is a market where there is one seller with lots of buyers.
______ refers to a situation where there are several 'sellers' of a particular good/services but only one buyer.
monopsony
A monopsony refers to a situation where there are several 'sellers' of a particular good/services but only one buyer.
______ refers to the forms of competition in a market.
Market structure
Market Structure Market structure refers to the forms of competition in a market.
______ is the simplest and most common in the market.
Price competition
Price and Non-price Competition Price competition is the simplest and most common in the market.
______ refer to confidential business information (whether favourable or negative) which provides and enterprise with a competitive edge.
Trade secrets
Trade Secrets Trade secrets refer to confidential business information (whether favourable or negative) which provides and enterprise with a competitive edge.
______ is the most basic form of competition and occurs on an 'all things being equal' basis.
Direct competition
Direct competition is the most basic form of competition and occurs on an 'all things being equal' basis.
______ is the agency responsible for the regulation of competition in any jurisdiction.
competition authority
The competition authority is the agency responsible for the regulation of competition in any jurisdiction.
______ is a duopoly or oligopoly which refer to the control of a market by two or a few undertakings respectively.
Closely related to the monopoly
Closely related to the monopoly is a duopoly or oligopoly which refer to the control of a market by two or a few undertakings respectively.
______ is the means of protecting intellectual property through various legal mechanisms whether statutory, tortious, equitable, economic etc.
Intellectual property law
Intellectual property law is the means of protecting intellectual property through various legal mechanisms whether statutory, tortious, equitable, economic etc.
